```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
  render = function(x, ...) {
    if (data.table::is.data.table(x) && !data.table::shouldPrint(x)) return(invisible(""))
    if (is.data.frame(x)) x <- knitr::kable(x, digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
    knitr::knit_print(x, ...)
  }
)
```

A NICHESObject is an S3 list with 15 slots, which you read with `$`. This guide
uses `NICHESv2_example`, a small spatial object with 80 synthetic cells.

```{r load}
library(NICHESv2)
library(data.table)

data(NICHESv2_example)
obj <- NICHESv2_example
dim(obj)
```

The object is a plain list, so functions return a changed copy. Always assign the
result back: `obj <- add_meta_column(obj, ...)`.

## Why long format

Most cell pairs carry no signal for most LR pairs. NICHESv2 stores only non-zero
values, in keyed `data.table`s with one row per value. Memory use then follows how
much signal exists, not how many combinations are possible.

## Cell slots

| Slot | Contents |
|---|---|
| `$cell.list` | Cell barcodes |
| `$cell.data` | Non-zero expression, one row per (cell, gene) |
| `$cell.meta` | One row per cell |

```{r cell}
head(obj$cell.data, 3)
```

In `$cell.data`, `score` is the value you supplied, and `score.norm` is its share
of that cell's total.

## Edge slots

An edge is one directed cell pair, with an ID of the form
`"SendingCell|ReceivingCell"`.

| Slot | Contents |
|---|---|
| `$edge.list` | One row per edge |
| `$edge.data` | Non-zero scores, one row per (edge, LRM) |
| `$edge.meta` | One row per edge, with both cells' metadata |

```{r edge}
head(obj$edge.data, 3)
```

An LRM ID has the form `"ligand|receptor"`. With the default
`normalize.method = "prop"`, `score.norm` is that LRM's share of the edge's total
score.

`$edge.meta` adds `Sending.` and `Receiving.` versions of each metadata column,
plus `Joint.` columns for text columns:

```{r edge-meta}
obj$edge.meta[, .(edges = .N), by = Joint.celltype][order(-edges)][1:3]
```

## Neighborhood slots

These are filled in when the object is built, and all three are indexed by cell.

| Slot | Contents |
|---|---|
| `$neighborhood.cell.list` | Each cell's neighbors |
| `$neighborhood.edge.list` | The edges in each cell's neighborhood |
| `$neighborhood.meta` | Neighbor and edge counts per cell |

```{r neighborhood}
head(obj$neighborhood.meta, 3)
```

By default, a neighborhood holds every edge whose two cells are both in that
neighborhood. `add_neighborhoods(overwrite = TRUE)` changes this:

| `edge.filter.mode` | Edges kept for a focal cell |
|---|---|
| `"both_in_neighborhood"` (default) | Both cells are the focal cell or its neighbors |
| `"any_in_neighborhood"` | At least one cell is the focal cell or a neighbor |
| `"central_cell_only"` | One cell is the focal cell |

## Gene and LRM slots

| Slot | Contents |
|---|---|
| `$gene.list`, `$gene.meta` | Genes and any annotations |
| `$LRM.list`, `$LRM.meta` | LR pairs and their annotations |

```{r lrm}
head(obj$LRM.meta, 3)
```

## Extras

`$aggregations` starts empty and is filled by `aggregate_NICHESObject()`.
`$segmentation` holds optional cell polygons, added with `add_segmentation()`.

## Attributes

Four attributes record how the object was built:

```{r attributes}
attr(obj, "mode")
attr(obj, "sample.col")
attr(obj, "edge.filter.mode")
attr(obj, "remove.autocrine")
```

## Changing metadata

To add or change one column, use `add_meta_column()` with values named by barcode:

```{r add-column}
region <- setNames(
  ifelse(obj$cell.meta$x > 0.5, "right", "left"),
  obj$cell.meta$cell
)
obj <- add_meta_column(obj, "region", region, verbose = FALSE)
obj$edge.meta[, .(edges = .N), by = Sending.region]
```

`add_cell_meta()` replaces the whole table, so any column you leave out is lost,
including coordinates. Use it only when you mean to replace everything.

## Subsetting

`obj[cells]` takes a vector of barcodes. Each kept cell keeps its neighborhood
entries and aggregation rows unchanged, while the edge slots keep only edges
between kept cells.

```{r subset}
type.a <- obj$cell.meta[celltype == "TypeA", cell]
sub <- obj[type.a]
dim(sub)
```

The [aggregation guide](aggregation.html) explains how to work with subsets.

## Merging

`merge_NICHESObjects()` combines objects from separate runs. They must share a mode
and have no barcodes in common. The merged object has no neighborhoods or
aggregations, so run `add_neighborhoods()` afterward. To process several samples
in one step, use `sample.col` in `create_NICHESObject()` instead.
